stops.note: The NPS dining page for Grand Canyon says that, due to the 2026 Bright Angel Creek flash flood and Stage 4 water restrictions, many restaurants are closed or have shortened hours until further notice, and it marks the Deli at the Marketplace and the Yavapai Dining Hall as closed. Tusayan, the gateway town 7 miles south of the park, has its own restaurants. Our advice: check the NPS page the morning of your visit, carry lunch on rim and trail days, and treat the Tusayan places below as the dependable fallback.

eats.name: Bright Angel Fountain
eats.what_to_order: Coffee, tea and breakfast in the morning, then ice cream and grab-and-go items in the afternoon, per the NPS listing.
eats.why: A canyon-side patio inside Bright Angel Lodge in Grand Canyon Village, handy for a quick bite before a rim walk or the Bright Angel Trail.
eats.hours_note: NPS lists it as open year-round at Bright Angel Lodge, with the park-wide warning that many restaurants are closed or on shortened hours; grandcanyonlodges.com says carry-out is available from the Fountain. No hours are stated on either page.
eats.open_evidence: NPS Grand Canyon dining page, which references the 2026 season, lists it as operating and not closed (viewed 2026-10-03); the lodging concessionaire's dining page also lists it, undated.
eats.source_name: National Park Service, Grand Canyon dining page

eats.name: Maswik Food Court and Pizza Pub
eats.what_to_order: The NPS page lists a food court and a pizza pub serving breakfast, lunch and dinner; the lodging concessionaire describes freshly baked pizzas and salads at the Pizza Pub.
eats.why: The casual, no-reservation option in the southwest corner of Grand Canyon Village at Maswik Lodge, when El Tovar is booked or you just want a quick meal.
eats.hours_note: NPS lists it as serving breakfast, lunch and dinner but warns that many restaurants are closed or on shortened hours until further notice; no hours are stated. grandcanyonlodges.com says the Food Court is open for dine-in (page undated).
eats.open_evidence: NPS Grand Canyon dining page, which references the 2026 season, lists it without a closure marker (viewed 2026-10-03); grandcanyonlodges.com lists it as open for dine-in, undated.
eats.source_name: National Park Service, Grand Canyon dining page

eats.name: Plaza Bonita
eats.what_to_order: Mexican plates across breakfast, lunch and dinner menus; the page lists entrees from about $19.99 at lunch to $30.99 at dinner but names no individual dishes.
eats.why: In Tusayan, 7 miles south of the park, not inside it; a sit-down Mexican restaurant with a breakfast menu, useful on a rim-day base.
eats.open_evidence: Own website shows current breakfast, lunch and dinner menus with prices and online ordering; the footer shows 2025 and the page states no hours, so this is moderate evidence (viewed 2026-10-03). The NPS dining page also lists Plaza Bonita among Tusayan restaurants.

eats.name: Big E Spaghetti Western
eats.what_to_order: Pappardelle Elk Ragu, Big E Homestead Lasagna and Campfire Carbonara are named on the menu page; steaks include the Trail Boss Ribeye.
eats.why: In Tusayan, 7 miles south of the park, not inside it; an Italian-and-steak dinner stop with a full bar (the NPS page still lists it by its earlier name, Big-E Steakhouse, with the same phone number).
eats.hours_note: Own site says open daily 3PM to 9PM; it notes limited availability of the lasagna.
eats.open_evidence: Own website (bigesteakhouse.com redirects to bigespaghettiwestern.com) lists daily hours, a current priced menu and contact details; the page shows no year (viewed 2026-10-03). The NPS dining page lists Big-E Steakhouse at the same phone number.

eats.name: Big John's Texas BBQ
eats.what_to_order: Beef brisket, pork ribs, hot links or BBQ nachos, all named on the restaurant's site.
eats.why: A no-reservations barbecue stop in Page with live music nightly from 6:30 to 9 PM, per its own site.
eats.hours_note: Open 7 days a week 11 AM to 9 PM, first-come first-served with no reservations, per own site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menu with a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: The Dam Bar & Grille
eats.what_to_order: San Juan River Jambalaya, Honey Jalapeno Salmon, Prime Rib or a Top Sirloin, all listed with prices on its site.
eats.why: A Page dining room with a 30-foot etched glass wall and a scaled-down model of Glen Canyon Dam, per its own site; the Page Chamber of Commerce also lists it.
eats.hours_note: Own site says open 7 days a week, 11am to 11pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website (damplaza.com) lists daily hours and a current priced menu with a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03); the Page Chamber of Commerce dining page also lists it, undated.

stops.note: The Navajo Nation Parks page for Monument Valley says the park offers limited food options: a restaurant at the visitor center is listed for summer months only, and Navajo vendors sell native food at roadside stands one mile before the visitor center. Our advice: do not count on eating inside the park in autumn or winter; plan meals in Kayenta, the nearest town with sit-down options I could verify, and carry water and snacks for the scenic drive.

eats.name: Amigo Cafe
eats.what_to_order: The cafe's site describes Mexican, Native American and American food and posts a breakfast menu and a coffee menu (as images).
eats.why: In the Navajo Nation town of Kayenta, not at Monument Valley itself; a family-run cafe that its own site says was established in 1983.
eats.hours_note: Open Tuesday to Saturday only, so closed Sunday and Monday. The cafe's home page says 8am to 8pm Tuesday-Saturday; its menu page says 10:30am to 8pm Tuesday-Friday and 8am to 8pm Saturday.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and posts menu images labelled 2024; the pages show no copyright year, so this is moderate evidence (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Coffee Pot Restaurant
eats.what_to_order: One of its 101 omelette combinations, or huevos rancheros, biscuits and gravy or pancakes, all named on its site.
eats.why: A West Sedona breakfast stop on the route toward Oak Creek Canyon, serving breakfast all day.
eats.hours_note: Open seven days a week, 6:00 AM to 2:00 PM, breakfast all day with lunch from 11:00 AM, per own site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menu with a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Indian Gardens Cafe & Market
eats.what_to_order: The breakfast burrito or the Dan the Man sandwich, both named in a Feb 2026 Sedona Lifestyles Magazine feature.
eats.why: A historic general store and cafe in Oak Creek Canyon, north of Uptown Sedona on State Route 89A, so it fits a day on the canyon's trails and swimming spots.
eats.hours_note: Open every day 8am to 4pm with the kitchen closing at 3pm, plus a Friday pizza night 4 to 8pm, per own site; the magazine feature puts most items between $11 and $17.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and a Friday pizza night (page shows no year); a Sedona Lifestyles Magazine feature dated 2026-02-08 describes the same hours and menu (viewed 2026-10-03).
eats.source_name: Venue's own website, with dishes per Sedona Lifestyles Magazine (2026-02-08)

eats.name: Mesa Grill
eats.what_to_order: Grilled steaks, fresh seafood or fish and chips with sidewinders; chilaquiles and biscuits and gravy are on the day menu.
eats.why: A full-service grill with a dinner menu from 3 PM, at 1185 Airport Rd in Sedona, a short way outside the Uptown area.
eats.hours_note: Own site says daily 7:30 AM to 9:00 PM, with breakfast, brunch and lunch to 3:00 PM and dinner from 3:00 PM; reservations by phone or OpenTable.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current daily hours and menu, takes reservations and shows no closure notice; the page shows no copyright year, so this is moderate evidence (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: The Fry Bread House
eats.what_to_order: Fry bread in its red chili, deluxe, chocolate and sugar versions; a second site mentions fry bread tacos.
eats.why: A Tohono O'odham-founded fry bread restaurant on N 7th Ave in central Phoenix that calls itself a James Beard Award winner; breads are made to order, so allow 10-15 minutes.
eats.hours_note: Open 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM Monday through Saturday and closed Sundays, per own site; bread is made to order and takes 10-15 minutes.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and a made-to-order notice; a second official site, azfrybreadhouse.com, cites New Times Best of Phoenix awards for 2022 to 2024; neither page shows a copyright year (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: FnB
eats.what_to_order: The homepage names no dishes; the menu is on the restaurant's own site.
eats.why: A full-service restaurant on 5th Ave in Old Town Scottsdale, and the dinner named in the itinerary; reservations are taken through Tock.
eats.hours_note: Full-service dining 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday, per own site, so closed Sunday and Monday.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current dining hours and a reservation link with a footer reading 2015-2026 (viewed 2026-10-03).

stops.note: Tucson Foodie reported on 2026-09-30 that Agustin Kitchen at Mercado San Agustin closed permanently, and that Presta Coffee Roasters, Seis Kitchen and La Estrella Bakery remain open in the courtyard. Our advice: the itinerary's Mercado San Agustin lunch still works, but pick one of the open tenants and check hours first.

eats.name: El Güero Canelo
eats.what_to_order: A Sonoran hot dog or carne asada, which its site calls its famous items, plus tacos, burritos and tortas.
eats.why: A Tucson Sonoran-hot-dog institution since 1993 with three Tucson branches, so one is usually on your way.
eats.hours_note: Own site lists 11 AM to 10 PM Sunday-Thursday and 11 AM to 11 PM Friday-Saturday, with slightly different closing times at some branches.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists three current Tucson locations with hours and online ordering, and mentions James Beard recognition; the page shows no copyright year (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: El Charro Cafe
eats.what_to_order: Chimichanga, tamales, enchiladas or carne seca, all named on its site.
eats.why: Its site says it is the nation's oldest Mexican restaurant in continuous operation by the same family, founded in 1922; the downtown branch is at 311 N Court Ave.
eats.hours_note: Downtown branch lists Monday to Sunday 11:00am to 9:00pm, per own site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current locations and the downtown hours, but its footer shows only 2023, so the year evidence is weak; Visit Tucson's downtown dining page also lists it, undated (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Cup Cafe
eats.what_to_order: The dessert carousel, a display of house-made sweets that the hotel's site highlights.
eats.why: Inside the historic Hotel Congress, open since 1990 per the hotel's site, so it suits a downtown stop in the evening or at brunch.
eats.hours_note: Open Monday to Sunday 8 AM to 9 PM and closed 2 to 4 PM daily; reservations are accepted for breakfast and lunch Monday-Thursday only, per own site.
eats.open_evidence: Hotel Congress's own page lists current hours and reservation rules with a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03); Visit Tucson's downtown dining page also lists it.

eats.name: Seis Kitchen
eats.what_to_order: The source names no menu items.
eats.why: A courtyard business at Mercado San Agustin, the market the itinerary names for lunch, reported by Tucson Foodie on 2026-09-30 as still open after a neighbouring restaurant closed.
eats.open_evidence: Tucson Foodie article dated 2026-09-30 lists Seis Kitchen among the Mercado San Agustin courtyard businesses that remain open (viewed 2026-10-03); its own site returned 403 to my fetch, so no hours were seen.

eats.name: Degnan's Kitchen
eats.what_to_order: The Yosemite Hospitality page lists deli sandwiches, artisan pizzas, breakfast favorites, coffee and espresso drinks and baked goods.
eats.why: A quick breakfast or trail-lunch stop in Yosemite Village, close to the Valley visitor facilities, with indoor seating and an outdoor deck.
eats.hours_note: Per travelyosemite.com (no year shown): breakfast daily 7-11am, lunch daily 11:30am-6pm, limited service 11-11:30am. The NPS lists it as year-round.
eats.open_evidence: NPS Yosemite dining page, dated June 1, 2026, lists it among Valley options open year-round (the page calls it Degnan's Bakery); the concessioner's yosemite.com page carries a 2026 copyright (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Base Camp Eatery
eats.what_to_order: The NPS describes a food court with a variety of breakfast, lunch and dinner selections; it does not name dishes.
eats.why: The year-round food court at Yosemite Valley Lodge, handy for a flexible meal near the Yosemite Falls end of the Valley when you are between trails.
eats.open_evidence: NPS Yosemite dining page, dated June 1, 2026, lists it as a year-round food court at Yosemite Valley Lodge (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Mountain Room
eats.what_to_order: The NPS describes upscale casual dinner; it does not name dishes.
eats.why: The sit-down dinner option at Yosemite Valley Lodge for a post-hike meal without leaving the Valley.
eats.open_evidence: NPS Yosemite dining page, dated June 1, 2026, lists Mountain Room as year-round upscale casual dinner (viewed 2026-10-03). No restaurant-owned page was fetched.

stops.note: The NPS says Tioga Road is typically open to vehicles from late May or June until sometime in November and is closed to vehicles for the winter, and that services along it are limited (bring your own food and water). Mono County's tourism listing says Whoa Nellie Deli is open late April through early October. Our advice: do the Tioga Road day in summer or early autumn, and pack lunch for Tuolumne Meadows.

eats.name: Whoa Nellie Deli
eats.what_to_order: The deli's own site calls out its world-famous fish tacos; the Mono County listing also mentions sandwiches, pizza and desserts.
eats.why: A restaurant inside the Tioga Gas Mart at the junction of Tioga Pass (Hwy 120) and US 395, right at Yosemite's east entrance, with outdoor patio and live music twice weekly per the county listing.
eats.hours_note: SEASONAL. Mono County's tourism listing says open late April through early October, so it may already be closed or about to close for the winter. The site lists daily 6:30am-9:00pm in season. Call (760) 647-1088 before relying on it.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists daily hours 6:30am-9pm and marks its 30th anniversary (open since 1996, so 2026), with no closure notice (viewed 2026-10-03); the Mono County tourism listing gives the seasonal dates.
eats.source_name: Mono County Tourism listing (venue's own site also checked)

eats.name: Nicely's Restaurant
eats.what_to_order: The chamber page names homemade sausage, soups and classic fried chicken, plus daily specials and desserts.
eats.why: A full-service breakfast, lunch and dinner restaurant with a bar and patio at Highway 395 and Fourth Street in the middle of Lee Vining.
eats.hours_note: Chamber page lists daily 7am-8pm; no seasonal closure is stated on the page.
eats.open_evidence: Lee Vining Chamber of Commerce listing shows current hours and menu highlights, but the page carries no year, so this is weaker evidence; confirm hours before a late-season visit (viewed 2026-10-03).

stops.note: The NPS lists Grant Grove Village's food services as a restaurant and a market; no other dining is named on its Goods & Services page. Our advice: the village is where you sleep on both nights, so plan on these two plus anything you bring; pack lunch for Mist Falls and grove days.

eats.name: Grant Grove Restaurant
eats.what_to_order: The operator's page lists omelets, eggs, pancakes and burritos at breakfast, and salads, burgers, sandwiches and pizzas at lunch and dinner.
eats.why: The village's sit-down restaurant, overlooking Bradley Meadow and the giant sequoias, with a walk-up window for to-go items.
eats.hours_note: Operator page: breakfast 7-10am, lunch and dinner 11:30am-8pm daily; the courtyard walk-up window is seasonal.
eats.open_evidence: Operator's page (DNC Parks & Resorts at SEKI) carries a 2026 copyright and lists current hours and menu; NPS Grant Grove Restaurant page updated December 18, 2025 (viewed 2026-10-03).
eats.source_name: DNC Parks & Resorts at SEKI (park concessioner)

eats.name: Grant Grove Market
eats.what_to_order: The NPS describes a small supermarket selling basic groceries, beer, wine and camping supplies, useful for building a picnic.
eats.why: The only other food source in the village, for trail lunches and supplies when you are staying in the park.
eats.open_evidence: NPS Grant Grove page, last updated August 31, 2025, describes the market; no hours or 2026 confirmation were found, so check ahead (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
eats.what_to_order: The site lists merchants including El Porteno Empanadas, Far West Fungi, Imperial Tea Court and Nopa Fish.
eats.why: An indoor food hall of nearly 50 local artisan food merchants right on the Embarcadero waterfront, which is on the Day 1 route.
eats.hours_note: Marketplace open daily 6am-10pm but individual merchants keep their own hours; closed Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day. Farmers market year-round Tue and Thu 10am-2pm, Sat 8am-2pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website carries a 2026 copyright and lists current hours and merchants, with no closure notice (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: La Palma Mexicatessen
eats.what_to_order: The site lists carnitas, chicharron, chile verde, chile colorado and pollo en salsa ranchera, plus handmade tortillas and tamales.
eats.why: A Mission District tortilla factory and take-out counter at 2884 24th Street, founded in 1953 per its site, matching the Day 2 Mission taqueria plan.
eats.hours_note: Site says closed Tuesdays and open daily in December; standard hours 8am-5pm. Outdoor seating weather permitting.
eats.open_evidence: Own website carries a 2026 copyright and lists current hours and holiday closures (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Mandalay
eats.what_to_order: James Beard Foundation notes tea leaf salad prepared tableside, samusa soup and the Mandalay special noodle in coconut broth.
eats.why: A Burmese restaurant in the Richmond District (4348 California St, a short ride from Golden Gate Park) that has operated since 1984.
eats.hours_note: Own site: Mon and Wed-Thu 4:30-8:30pm; Fri-Sun 11:30am-3pm and 4:30-8:30pm; closed Tuesdays.
eats.open_evidence: James Beard Foundation announced it as a 2024 America's Classics winner, and its own website currently lists hours with no closure notice, though the page shows no year (viewed 2026-10-03).
eats.source_name: James Beard Foundation (restaurant's own site mandalaysf.com also checked)

eats.name: Oxbow Public Market
eats.what_to_order: The market's site lists vendors including Hog Island Oyster Bar, Ritual Coffee Roasters, Live Fire Pizza, Loveski Deli, Fieldwork Brewing Company, Roman Holiday Gelato and Johnny Doughnuts.
eats.why: The downtown Napa food hall on this itinerary's Day 3, with 20 vendors at 610 and 644 First Street, so a group can each eat something different.
eats.hours_note: Open daily 7:30am-9pm per the market's site; individual vendors may keep different hours.
eats.open_evidence: Own website carries a 2026 copyright and lists current hours and its 20 vendors (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Gillwoods Cafe
eats.what_to_order: The site mentions eggs Benedict and banana pecan pancakes.
eats.why: A breakfast and brunch cafe at 1313 Main Street, open since May 1991 per its site, that cooks from scratch.
eats.hours_note: Per its site: Tue-Wed 7am-2pm; Sun-Mon and Thu-Sat 7am-9pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and ordering links and says it opened May 1991, but the page shows no year; also listed in the City of St. Helena Dining Guide, which is undated (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Cafe Sarafornia
eats.what_to_order: The site mentions huevos rancheros, omelets and French toast.
eats.why: A family-run breakfast-and-lunch diner at 1413 Lincoln Avenue, operated by the Dierkhising family since 1976 per its site, within walking distance of downtown.
eats.hours_note: Per its site: Mon-Fri 8am-12:30pm; Sat-Sun 7:30am-2pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours, online ordering and 45-plus years under the same family, but the page shows no explicit year (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Buster's Original Southern BBQ
eats.what_to_order: The homepage describes authentic Louisiana barbecue but lists no specific dishes.
eats.why: A Calistoga barbecue stop in business since 1965 per its own site, good for lunch before the Old Faithful Geyser and mud bath stops.
eats.hours_note: Open daily 10am-8pm per its site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website carries a 2026 copyright and lists current hours and online ordering (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Calistoga Inn Restaurant & Brewery
eats.what_to_order: The site gives no dishes; it describes a restaurant, brewery and hotel at 1250 Lincoln Avenue.
eats.why: A casual restaurant and brewery in the middle of town, with breakfast, lunch, dinner and weekend brunch served.
eats.hours_note: Per its site: breakfast daily 9-11am; lunch 11am-4pm; dinner Sun-Thu 4-9pm, Fri-Sat 4-9:30pm; weekend brunch 9am-1pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and Resy booking, but the page shows no year (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Sam's No. 3
eats.what_to_order: The site highlights its pork green chili (made with Hatch, New Mexico chilies), breakfast burritos, pancakes, cheeseburgers and souvlaki.
eats.why: A Denver diner that the site says dates to 1927, with a green-chili-and-souvlaki menu of 100+ items that works for any meal of a road-trip day.
eats.hours_note: Three locations (Glendale, Downtown at 1500 Curtis St, Aurora). Per the site, Downtown is open 7am-2pm Mon-Tue and 7am until 8pm or later Wed-Sun; Glendale runs 7:30am-8:30pm Sun-Thu and to 9pm Fri-Sat. Check the site for the location you pick.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours for each location, online ordering, and recent posts dated 2026 (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Denver Central Market
eats.what_to_order: The page lists vendors including Vero (grain bowls, cortados), Izzio (gourmet pizza), Green Seed (salads), Tammens Fish Market and Temper Chocolates.
eats.why: A food hall at 2669 Larimer St in the RiNo Art District, so it fits the RiNo mural-walk day and lets a group order from several counters.
eats.hours_note: Food vendors Sun-Thu 8am-9pm, Fri-Sat 8am-11pm; Curio Bar hours differ. Individual vendors may keep their own hours.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current food-vendor hours and a named vendor lineup (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no clear year.

eats.name: Ratio Beerworks
eats.what_to_order: The page lists the taproom's beer; it does not name food at the RiNo taproom (food is named only for the separate Overland location).
eats.why: A RiNo taproom at 2920 Larimer St, and one of the two breweries the Denver itinerary names for day 2.
eats.hours_note: RiNo taproom hours per site: Mon-Wed 12pm-11pm, Thu-Fri 12pm-12am, Sat 11am-12am, Sun 11am-11pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current RiNo taproom hours seven days a week (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year.

eats.name: Hop Alley
eats.what_to_order: Per Visit Denver, Shanghai rice cakes, beef chow fun and Beijing duck rolls; the venue's own page lists traditional Chinese menus including vegan and vegetarian.
eats.why: A RiNo Chinese restaurant, a good sit-down dinner after the day-2 mural and brewery walk.
eats.hours_note: Monday-Saturday 5-10pm, closed Sundays; reservations via OpenTable.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours, a Chef's Counter residency, reservation and takeout ordering details, and 2025 award notices (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: The Golden Diner
eats.what_to_order: The site lists pancakes, omelets and scrambles, Braised Pork Benedict and the Colorado Loco Moco.
eats.why: A locally owned breakfast diner at 700 12th St, a few minutes' walk from Washington Avenue, before the Coors tour and Red Rocks.
eats.hours_note: Open daily 7am-2pm-ish per the site; closes at noon on Christmas Eve and all day Christmas Day.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists daily hours and a Christmas closure notice (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year, only that it has served breakfast 'for the past 15 years'.

eats.name: Cafe 13
eats.what_to_order: The site lists all-day breakfast, lunch from 11am (sandwiches, salads and soups) and pastries baked daily.
eats.why: In the historic Armory building at 1301 Arapahoe St, one block west of Washington Avenue; it is open into the evening on Friday and Saturday.
eats.hours_note: Per the site: Mon-Thu 6:30am-3pm, Fri 6:30am-8pm, Sat 7:30am-8pm, Sun 7:30am-3pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours, online ordering and a '2025' copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03); Visit Golden also carries a listing.

eats.name: Golden City Brewery
eats.what_to_order: The page says a food truck is on site but does not name dishes; the brewery describes itself as Golden's original microbrewery.
eats.why: A Golden microbrewery that the site says has been pouring since 1993, a few blocks from the Colorado School of Mines.
eats.hours_note: Opens daily at 11am. The page states summer last-call times of 8:30pm Sun-Thu and 9:30pm Fri-Sat; no winter hours are stated, so check before a cold-season visit.
eats.open_evidence: Own website shows hours, a food truck listing and a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Village Coffee Shop
eats.what_to_order: The site lists fluffy pancakes, a green chili smothered breakfast burrito, hand-crafted burgers and French toast.
eats.why: A small Boulder diner at 1605 Folsom St that the site says has served the town for over 55 years, with breakfast all day.
eats.hours_note: Open 7am-2pm daily per the site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current daily hours and menu (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year, so this is weaker evidence than a dated page.

eats.name: The Sink
eats.what_to_order: The site lists the Texas Onion Straw Burger, Portabella burger, Cowboy Reuben, pizzas and barbecue short ribs.
eats.why: A single-location Boulder bar-and-burger landmark at 1165 13th St that the site says dates to 1923, near Pearl Street and the University of Colorado campus.
eats.hours_note: Sun-Thu 11am-10pm, Fri-Sat 11am-11pm per the site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours, a menu and current weekly specials such as Pizza Tuesdays (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year.

eats.name: Boulder Dushanbe Teahouse
eats.what_to_order: The site lists brunch, lunch, dinner, tea time and an Afternoon Tea & Dim Sum Tea service; it names no individual dishes on the homepage.
eats.why: A teahouse at 1770 13th St, with brunch on weekends and a tea service between lunch and dinner.
eats.hours_note: Mon-Fri lunch 11am-3pm, teatime 3-5pm, dinner 5-9pm; Sat-Sun brunch 8am-3pm. The page lists private-event closures on October 2, 4, 8, 10 and 24 (no year shown), so check the site for the date you plan to visit.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours, upcoming private-event closure dates and a 'Copyright 2026' footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Silver Grill Cafe
eats.what_to_order: The site names its cinnamon rolls (with a rotating Roll of the Month), pancakes, hash browns, country fried steak, burgers and skillets.
eats.why: A single-location Old Town breakfast place at 218 Walnut St that describes itself as Fort Collins' oldest restaurant, open since 1933.
eats.hours_note: Open daily 7am-2pm per the site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists daily hours and a 2025 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03); Visit Fort Collins also featured it in an October 2024 dining roundup.

eats.name: UNION Bar & Soda Fountain
eats.what_to_order: The site lists a double-patty burger, Monte Cristo sandwiches, French toast, house-made sodas and shakes.
eats.why: A soda-fountain-style diner at 250 Jefferson St, a short walk from Old Town Square, with vegan and gluten-free options marked on the menu.
eats.hours_note: Mon-Fri 11am to close, Sat-Sun 10am to close per the site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menu with a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: CooperSmith's Pub & Brewing
eats.what_to_order: The site lists full dinners and patio dining with vegetarian options and regional specialties, alongside its house ales, lagers and stouts.
eats.why: An Old Town Square brewpub that the site says has operated since 1989, a walkable dinner after the New Belgium and Odell visits.
eats.hours_note: Brewpub Sun-Wed 11am-9pm, Thu-Sat 11am-10pm per the site; the separate billiards room opens at 3pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current brewpub hours and a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Versailles
eats.what_to_order: Cuban sandwiches, croquetas and vaca frita, plus Cuban coffee from the walk-up ventanita window.
eats.why: A Little Havana Cuban restaurant on Calle Ocho (3555 SW 8th St) that says it has served the community since 1971, with a bakery and a coffee window for a quick stop between South Beach and Little Havana.
eats.hours_note: Own website lists Monday-Thursday 8am-midnight, Friday-Saturday 8am-1am, Sunday 9am-midnight; the Miami tourism board listing gives later closing times, so confirm before a late visit. The tourism board says reservations are not accepted for parties under 15.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menu and the Greater Miami tourism board listing carries the same address and ventanita; neither page shows a year (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Robert Is Here
eats.what_to_order: A hand-blended milkshake or smoothie made with fresh fruit.
eats.why: A Homestead fruit stand that says it began in 1959, with tropical fruit you will not find at a supermarket, a free petting zoo and picnic facilities on the way between Miami and the Everglades.
eats.hours_note: Own website says open every day 9am-6pm, closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists daily hours and its in-season produce collection shows a last-updated stamp of 2026-09-28 (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Triad Seafood Market & Café
eats.what_to_order: Stone crab (its site promotes all-you-can-eat stone crab starting October 15) or the fried-conch sandwich that Florida Rambler mentions.
eats.why: A family seafood market and café at 401 W School Dr that says it has operated since 1984, with screened outdoor dining overlooking the river per Florida Rambler.
eats.hours_note: Seasonal. Its own site gives an opening date of October 1, 2026 and says hours vary with tourist season and seafood availability, and advises calling ahead (239-695-2662) to confirm hours and stone crab availability. Florida Rambler gives stone crab season as October 15 to May 1.
eats.open_evidence: Own website states an October 1, 2026 opening date and advertises all-you-can-eat stone crab beginning October 15; Florida Rambler's stone crab article (published September 14, 2026, updated September 27, 2026) also lists it (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Camellia Street Grill
eats.what_to_order: Fresh fish and stone crab; its site says it specializes in fresh stone crab and local seafood.
eats.why: An open-air spot at 202 Camellia St with riverside seating and, per Florida Rambler, live bluegrass on Saturday nights.
eats.hours_note: Own website lists Monday-Sunday 11am-9pm and shows no seasonal notice, but its page carries a 2023 copyright; stone crab season runs October 15 to May 1 per Florida Rambler. Confirm hours by phone (239-695-2003).
eats.open_evidence: Listed with its address in Florida Rambler's stone crab article (published September 14, 2026, updated September 27, 2026); own website lists hours and lunch and dinner menus but is copyrighted 2023 (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: No Name Pub
eats.what_to_order: Pizza and fish dip, which its site says it is known best for.
eats.why: A Lower Keys landmark at 30813 Watson Blvd that its site says began as a general store and bait shop in 1931 and became a restaurant in 1936, with walls covered in autographed dollar bills.
eats.hours_note: Own website lists Monday-Sunday 11am-10pm; no closure or storm notice on the page.
eats.open_evidence: Own website carries a 2026 copyright and lists current daily hours (viewed 2026-10-03).

stops.note: Blue Heaven's own site says it is closed for vacation September 8 to October 15, 2026. Our read: only one Key West eat could be confirmed from a current source in this research pass, so the list is thin. Our advice: if you arrive before mid-October, look up other Old Town options and check their hours first.

eats.name: Blue Heaven
eats.what_to_order: The page we read names no dishes; it lists breakfast and lunch from 8am, a happy hour and a dinner service.
eats.why: A Key West restaurant at 729 Thomas St that serves breakfast and lunch on a first-come, first-served basis and takes limited dinner reservations.
eats.hours_note: CLOSED for vacation September 8 to October 15, 2026 per its own site. Otherwise breakfast and lunch 8am-2:30pm, happy hour 3:30-5pm, dinner 5-10pm; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
eats.open_evidence: Own website posts a 2026 vacation closure with a reopening after October 15 and lists current hours (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Gideon's Bakehouse (Disney Springs)
eats.what_to_order: Cookies; the page currently features The Frankenstein and The Bride of Frankenstein.
eats.why: An Orlando-founded bakery with a second shop in Disney Springs, close to the Lake Buena Vista hotels; the page says the Disney Springs shop takes no preorders.
eats.hours_note: Disney Springs shop: Sunday-Thursday 10am-11pm, Friday-Saturday 10am-11:30pm, listed as open 365 days; no preorders there. The original East End Market shop (3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando) is 10am-7pm daily, closed on major holidays.
eats.open_evidence: Own website carries a 2026 copyright and lists current hours for both shops (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Café Tu Tu Tango
eats.what_to_order: Small plates such as Jamon Serrano Croquetas, Crispy Brussels Sprouts and Sesame Steak Skewers.
eats.why: A single-location tapas restaurant at 8625 International Drive that says it has operated for over 30 years, with live entertainment nightly and during brunch.
eats.hours_note: Own website lists Monday-Friday 11am-midnight, Saturday 10am-midnight, Sunday 10am-11pm; weekend brunch from 10am.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menu (page shows no year); Orlando Weekly's feature on long-running restaurants, published July 2, 2026, lists it at 8625 International Drive (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Coconuts On The Beach
eats.what_to_order: Locally sourced seafood, grilled and seasoned, and its signature tropical cocktails.
eats.why: Oceanfront dining in Cocoa Beach with live local bands through the week, per its site.
eats.open_evidence: Own website carries a 2026 copyright, describes live bands and oceanfront dining, and offers online ordering and gift cards (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Florida's Seafood Bar & Grill
eats.what_to_order: Dynamite Shrimp, Shrimp Volcano or Snow Crab.
eats.why: Run since 1997 by owners Nick and Holly Zervos at 480 W Cocoa Beach Causeway, with an oyster bar and a shrimp-focused menu.
eats.hours_note: Own website lists Monday-Thursday 11:30am-9pm, Friday-Saturday 11:30am-9:30pm, Sunday noon-9pm; lunch service Monday-Saturday only, 11:30am-3pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menu with no storm or closure notice; the page refers to a 2025 award, so it was edited in 2025 or later (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Dixie Crossroads
eats.what_to_order: Rock shrimp, bacon shrimp and the corn fritters served with meals.
eats.why: In Titusville at 1475 Garden St rather than Cocoa Beach itself; it says it has operated since 1983 and serves wild ocean-caught seafood from Port Canaveral.
eats.hours_note: Own website lists 11am-9pm daily, closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists daily hours and online ordering (page shows no year); Florida Backroads Travel's page, last updated May 15, 2026, gives the same hours (viewed 2026-10-03).
eats.source_name: Venue's own website; Florida Backroads Travel

eats.name: Jordan's Restaurant
eats.what_to_order: Maine blueberry products, which the site says the restaurant specialises in; the site lists breakfast and lunch menus.
eats.why: A local, home-style breakfast counter at 80 Cottage Street started by the Paine family in 1976, and one of the earliest openers in town at 5 AM.
eats.hours_note: Own site lists open daily 5:00 AM-2:00 PM and gives no closing dates; the Bar Harbor chamber listing describes it as open seasonally without stating dates.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists daily hours, a current breakfast/lunch menu with an ordering system, and says it is celebrating its 50th anniversary (1976 + 50 = 2026) (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound
eats.what_to_order: Lobster rolls, which the site calls a fan favorite, or steamed lobsters, clams and mussels.
eats.why: A family lobster pound in Trenton on the mainland approach to Mount Desert Island, operating since 1956 per its site.
eats.hours_note: In-season retail and dine-in dates listed as June 21, 2026 through October 25, 2026; the site lists off-season hours of Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM with Saturday call ahead.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists 2026 in-season dates running through October 25, 2026, plus current off-season hours (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Becky's Diner
eats.what_to_order: Breakfast, lunch or dinner; the venue's page does not name specific dishes (full menu is a PDF on its site).
eats.why: A working-waterfront diner on Commercial Street serving since 1991 and opening at 5 AM.
eats.hours_note: Open 7 days a week 5AM-9PM; open until noon on July 4th and Christmas Eve; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and holiday closures (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year.

eats.name: Tandem Coffee + Bakery
eats.what_to_order: Cinnamon rolls and pies, which the site mentions among its baked goods.
eats.why: The Congress Street bakery counterpart to Tandem's Anderson Street roastery, in the Portland neighborhoods the itinerary walks on day 2.
eats.hours_note: Coffee + Bakery at 742 Congress St listed open 7 days a week 8am-1pm, with same-day online pickup ordering 7:45am-10:15am.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours at both locations and carries a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Duckfat
eats.what_to_order: Belgian-style frites, hand-punched and twice-fried in duck fat and served in cones.
eats.why: Portland's duck-fat frites spot at 43 Middle Street, operating since 2005 per its site.
eats.hours_note: Open daily 11AM-10PM; first come, first served.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current daily hours and both locations (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year.

eats.name: Eventide Oyster Co.
eats.what_to_order: The Brown Butter Lobster Roll, plus oysters and the fish sandwich, all named on the site.
eats.why: The oyster bar the Portland itinerary builds its day-1 dinner around, on Middle Street in the Old Port.
eats.hours_note: Open 7 days a week 11am-11pm; first come, first served with limited reservations through Resy; diners are asked to limit their time to 2 hours.
eats.open_evidence: Own Portland page lists hours and says it is currently booking reservations within 2 weeks of today's date (viewed 2026-10-03).

stops.note: Only two Freeport places are verified here: a lobster pound whose season ends October 12, 2026 and a brewery taproom. Check dates before relying on the lobster pound in autumn.

eats.name: Harraseeket Lunch & Lobster Co.
eats.what_to_order: Lobster rolls, clams and Maine shrimp, with whoopie pies and pies for dessert, all named on the site.
eats.why: A family-run waterfront lobster pound and lunch counter in South Freeport, running since 1970 per its site, with indoor and outdoor seating.
eats.hours_note: Seasonal, May through October: Thursday-Tuesday 11:00am-4:00pm, closed Wednesdays; the site gives the last day of the season as Columbus Day 10/12/2026; cash only (ATM on site).
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and states 'Last Day for Season: Columbus Day 10/12/2026' (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Maine Beer Company
eats.what_to_order: IPAs and pale ales, which the site says it is known for, plus seasonal releases such as Black Barn.
eats.why: Freeport's own brewery, founded in 2009, with a tasting room and bottle shop on US Route 1.
eats.hours_note: Tasting room open daily 11am-8pm Sun-Thurs and 11am-9pm Fri-Sat; bottle shop opens at 10am daily. The page gives no food policy.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current tasting room hours and carries a 2026 copyright notice (viewed 2026-10-03).

stops.note: Many Boothbay-area eateries are seasonal; the region's own dining directory tells visitors to check individual listings for hours and seasonal operation. Only two places that state year-round operation are verified here.

eats.name: Brady's
eats.what_to_order: Classic American cuisine; the page names no specific dishes.
eats.why: A Union Street restaurant that says it is open all year, handy when the harbor's seasonal places have closed.
eats.hours_note: Site says it is open all year; Monday closed, Tuesday-Saturday 11:30 AM-8:00 PM, Sunday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and says 'open all year long' (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year.

eats.name: Footbridge Brewery & BBQ
eats.what_to_order: Brisket sandwiches, burnt ends and steak pizza, with 20 beers on tap made from 90% Maine-grown ingredients.
eats.why: A Granary Way brewpub in the harbor area that states it operates year-round, with a pet-friendly patio.
eats.hours_note: Site lists open daily Noon-9PM and states it operates year-round.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists daily hours, says its menu was reworked over the summer, and lists an Oktoberfest event for 9/19 (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year.

eats.name: Camden Deli
eats.what_to_order: Breakfast pancakes and omelets, or a Reuben, panini or seafood chowder for lunch, all named on the site.
eats.why: A Camden landmark on Main Street since 1985 per its site, with a rooftop deck overlooking the harbor.
eats.hours_note: Open 7 days a week 7am-6pm; online ordering 7am-5:30pm.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and an active online ordering system (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year.

eats.name: Peter Ott's on the Water
eats.what_to_order: Fresh seafood with seasonal offerings; the page names no specific dishes.
eats.why: A harbor-front dinner spot at 16 Bayview Landing that suits the itinerary's harbor-front dinner.
eats.hours_note: Seasonal: site says open May-October, daily 11:30am-9:00pm; walk-ins welcome, reservations for groups of eight or more. Its sister Ott's Cafe is marked closed for the 2026 season. The exact October closing date is not stated.
eats.open_evidence: Own website says it is open for the 2026 season daily 11:30am-9:00pm and marks Ott's Cafe closed for 2026 (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Salt Wharf
eats.what_to_order: Oysters and hand-crafted cocktails, which the site mentions.
eats.why: A dockside bar-bistro on Camden harbor, opened in 2022, whose site describes year-round harborside dining and a rooftop patio.
eats.hours_note: Dining room Thursday-Monday 4-8 PM; rooftop/patio Friday-Monday 12-7 PM; closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current dining room and rooftop hours and describes year-round harborside dining (viewed 2026-10-03); the page shows no year other than its 2022 opening.

stops.note: Dining inside Big Bend is thin: the NPS dining page says the Mountain View Restaurant in the Chisos Basin is closed, with a food truck outside the main Lodge building; packaged food and drinks are sold at Castolon, the Chisos Basin and Rio Grande Village, and Hikers Lunches are available for picnicking. Full meals are outside the park in Terlingua and Study Butte. Our advice: plan trail-day food in advance.

eats.name: Espresso y Poco Mas
eats.what_to_order: Espresso drinks and breakfast burritos, with eggs Benedict variations, pancakes and French toast also listed.
eats.why: The listing calls it the only place in Terlingua for espresso and offers to-go orders aimed at early park departures.
eats.hours_note: Listed open daily 7:30 AM to 2 PM, including Christmas morning; to-go orders available
eats.open_evidence: Visit Big Bend (Brewster County Tourism Council, page footer 2026) lists current daily hours, phone and menu highlights (viewed 2026-10-03)
eats.source_name: Visit Big Bend (Brewster County Tourism Council)

eats.name: DB's Rustic Iron BBQ
eats.what_to_order: Prime-grade brisket, St. Louis-style pork ribs, smoked turkey breast, sausage or barbacoa.
eats.why: Central Texas-style post oak barbecue served in the Terlingua Ghost Town since 1993, which the listing says moved to a new permanent location in 2024.
eats.hours_note: Listed open Wednesday through Monday from 11 AM until sellout; closed Tuesdays
eats.open_evidence: Visit Big Bend (Brewster County Tourism Council, page footer 2026) lists current hours and notes the 2024 relocation to a new permanent location (viewed 2026-10-03)
eats.source_name: Visit Big Bend (Brewster County Tourism Council)

eats.name: Starlight Theatre Restaurant & Saloon
eats.what_to_order: Antelope tenders, quail, brisket tacos, the Diego burger or bourbon pecan pie.
eats.why: Dinner in a restored 1939 Chisos Mining Company movie house in the Terlingua Ghost Town, with live Texas singer-songwriters from around 6 PM.
eats.hours_note: Own site lists Sun-Fri 5:00 pm-12:00 am and Sat 5:00 pm-1:00 am; reservations recommended October through April
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and phone, and Visit Big Bend (Brewster County Tourism Council, footer 2026) lists dinner nightly from 5 PM with the same menu highlights (both viewed 2026-10-03)
eats.source_name: Visit Big Bend (Brewster County Tourism Council)

eats.name: Joe's Bakery & Coffee Shop
eats.what_to_order: Huevos Rancheros Plate, Joey Rocha Breakfast or Carne Guisada Plate.
eats.why: Family-run East Austin Tex-Mex breakfast counter that the site says has operated since 1962.
eats.hours_note: Closed Mondays; Tuesday-Sunday 6:00 AM-2:00 PM; closed on holidays; breakfast all day, lunch from 10:30 AM; does not accept Apple Pay or contactless payments
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours, menu prices and a 3% packaging fee notice (viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Franklin Barbecue
eats.what_to_order: Brisket, pork ribs, pulled pork, turkey or sausage.
eats.why: Its site says it uses USDA Prime brisket and heritage-breed pork and sells until sold out, typically 2-3 pm, with advance pre-orders available.
eats.hours_note: Tuesday-Sunday 11am until sold out (typically 2-3pm); closed Mondays; site lists closures Nov 26-27 and Dec 25-28
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours plus upcoming events dated Oct 16-18, 2026 and upcoming holiday closures (viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Matt's El Rancho
eats.what_to_order: Sizzling Angus beef fajitas, cheese enchiladas, pork tamales or Bob's Famous Queso.
eats.why: Single-location South Lamar Tex-Mex restaurant founded in 1952 that traces its roots to a 1923 tamale cart, per its own site.
eats.hours_note: Closed Tuesdays; Mon and Sun 11am-9pm, Wed-Thu 11am-10pm, Fri-Sat 11am-11pm
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menu with a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Old German Bakery & Restaurant
eats.what_to_order: Authentic German breads and pastries, or breakfast served throughout the day and the daily specials.
eats.why: Established in 1975 on West Main Street and owned since 1998 by Lutz Henschel, making traditional German recipes from scratch.
eats.hours_note: Directory lists Mon-Tue 7AM-2PM, Fri 7AM-2PM, Sat-Sun 7AM-3PM and closed Wednesday-Thursday; confirm before driving
eats.open_evidence: Fredericksburg Convention & Visitors Bureau directory (footer 2026) lists current hours, and its bakeries guide, last modified 2026-02-02, includes it (viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Der Lindenbaum
eats.what_to_order: Schnitzel, steaks or sandwiches, with apfel strudel, streuselkuchen or Black Forest cake for dessert.
eats.why: German cooking in a limestone building built by Fredericksburg's German pioneers; the chef-owner trained in Germany and opened it first as a bakery.
eats.hours_note: Closed Tuesdays; both the venue and the visitors bureau list lunch and dinner service on other days
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and Rheinland lunch specials, and the Fredericksburg Visitors Bureau directory (footer 2026) lists it with hours (both viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Naegelin's Bakery
eats.what_to_order: Kolaches (bratwurst, jalapeno sausage or fruit and cheese) and apple, cherry or peach strudel.
eats.why: Calls itself the oldest bakery in Texas, in business since 1868, a few steps off the New Braunfels plaza.
eats.hours_note: Monday-Friday 6:30AM-5:30PM, Saturday 6:30AM-5:00PM, Sunday 8:00AM-2:00PM
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and menus (viewed 2026-10-03); a New Braunfels Herald-Zeitung feature published 2024-11-01 describes it as operating and selling strudels and sweet pretzels

eats.name: Gristmill River Restaurant & Bar
eats.what_to_order: Beef Tenderloin Salad, GristBurger or Jack Daniel's Pecan Pie a la mode.
eats.why: Dining in the ruins of an 1878 cotton gin under Gruene's water tower above the Guadalupe River, open since 1977.
eats.hours_note: Sun-Thu 11 am-9 pm, Fri-Sat 11 am-10 pm; live music in the beer garden
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and a full priced menu, with a 2025 copyright footer and current hiring and holiday-party posts (viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Mi Tierra Cafe & Bakery
eats.what_to_order: The all-day breakfast of Tex-Mex, Mexican and American classics, or the comida corrida lunch specials.
eats.why: A Market Square landmark that grew from a three-table cafe in 1941, with a bakery counter.
eats.open_evidence: Own website (La Familia Cortez) announces La Gran Tamalada for September 22, 2026 at Market Square and lists current happy-hour times (viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Cowboy's Buffet & Steak Room

eats.name: The Canyon Diner
eats.what_to_order: Burgers, deli sandwiches or a fresh 7 or 15 inch pizza; the page also lists shrimp and halibut baskets.
eats.why: Quick, casual lunch about a mile from the park entrance, with online ordering for pickup if you want to eat at an overlook.

eats.name: Stone Hearth Grille
eats.what_to_order: Steaks and seafood from the grille; the page mentions rib eye, filet, pork chop and grilled halibut.
eats.why: A dinner-only grille in the neighbouring town of Tropic rather than Bryce Canyon City itself, on the way along Highway 12 — a step up from the diners if you want a sit-down evening.
eats.hours_note: Dinner only, open March 23-October 29, 2026 and closed for winter; reservations recommended (435-679-8923).
eats.open_evidence: Own website states 'Open March 23rd - October 29th 2026' and 'Reopening Mid-March 2026' (viewed 2026-10-03).

stops.note: Escalante is a small town, and only one eat here could be confirmed as currently operating for this guide. Visit Utah warns that along this corridor many restaurants are closed during the winter months. Our advice: check hours before relying on any meal, and carry snacks for Highway 12.

eats.name: Escalante Outfitters
eats.what_to_order: The pizza and beer the site features.
eats.why: An outfitter store, restaurant and beer stop in the middle of Escalante, so it doubles as a gear and trail-info stop for Grand Staircase-Escalante.
eats.hours_note: Restaurant 11 AM-9 PM daily and store 9 AM-9 PM daily per the site; it says 'Open for the 2026 Season' and does not state a closing date.
eats.open_evidence: Own homepage says 'Open for the 2026 Season!' and lists restaurant hours (viewed 2026-10-03).

stops.note: Boulder is a very small town on Highway 12 between Escalante and Torrey; only the two Hell's Backbone venues could be verified here. Visit Utah warns that many restaurants in this corridor close for the winter, and Hell's Backbone dinner requires a reservation.

eats.name: Little Bone Food Truck
eats.what_to_order: Breakfast or lunch from the truck; the page lists no individual dishes.
eats.why: The easy no-reservation option on a Highway 12 driving day, run by the Hell's Backbone Grill and Farm operation and serving from 7 AM.
eats.hours_note: Breakfast and lunch 7 AM-2 PM seven days a week; dinners Tuesday and Wednesday 4-8 PM.
eats.open_evidence: Hell's Backbone's own site lists these hours alongside 2026 events, including an October 14 and a November 2 event (viewed 2026-10-03).
eats.source_name: Hell's Backbone Grill & Farm (venue's own website)

eats.name: Hell's Backbone Grill
eats.what_to_order: Dinner service only; the page lists no dishes, and Visit Utah says the kitchen uses vegetables and herbs from the restaurant's own organic farm.
eats.why: A destination dinner on the Highway 12 route that pairs a grill with its own farm, worth planning the day around if you reserve ahead.
eats.hours_note: Dinner Thursday-Monday 4-9 PM; closed Tuesday and Wednesday; reservations required.
eats.open_evidence: Own site lists dinner hours, a reservation link and 2026 events (viewed 2026-10-03).
eats.source_name: Hell's Backbone Grill & Farm (venue's own website)

stops.note: Capitol Reef National Park has no restaurant or lodge, and the Gifford House in the park sells baked goods and snacks only, usually March through October. Our read: Torrey, just outside the park, is the realistic place to eat, so pack a picnic for trail days.

eats.name: Randy's at The Chuckwagon
eats.what_to_order: Full breakfast until 11 AM, then lunch; the Torrey town page lists the deli's Reubens and chicken salad sandwiches.
eats.why: An early, simple breakfast-and-lunch counter on Torrey's Main Street, handy for a Capitol Reef start or for a picnic lunch.
eats.hours_note: Open 7 AM-3 PM daily; breakfast served until 11 AM.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists 7 AM-3 PM daily hours and a 2026 copyright footer (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Broken Spur Inn & Steakhouse
eats.what_to_order: Hand-cut steaks; the page mentions the ribeye, sirloin and St. Louis ribs.
eats.why: Torrey's sit-down steakhouse about five minutes from Capitol Reef, per the town's own listing.
eats.hours_note: Dinner 4:30-10:00 PM daily from early March through mid-November; breakfast 7-10 AM daily, free for hotel guests and $12.99 for non-guests.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists seasonal dinner hours and a 2025 guest review (viewed 2026-10-03); the page carries no 2026 date.

eats.name: Moab Diner
eats.what_to_order: Sourdough French toast or a steak burrito, per Visit Utah.
eats.why: A retro diner on Main Street with an ice cream shop attached, serving diner food until 9 PM, so it covers both a pre-Arches breakfast and a late dinner.
eats.hours_note: Moab Happenings' restaurant guide lists Mon-Sat 6 AM-9 PM and closed Sundays; the venue's own site could not be fetched, so confirm before going.
eats.open_evidence: Visit Utah's Moab restaurants page lists it with a current description (viewed 2026-10-03); that page is undated, and the Moab Happenings guide independently lists its hours.

eats.name: Milt's Stop & Eat
eats.what_to_order: Per Visit Utah, the loaded Cowboy Burger, onion rings and a chocolate milkshake.
eats.why: Moab's oldest restaurant, first opened in September 1954 by Milt Galbraith, per its own site.
eats.hours_note: Open daily 11 AM to close, between 7 PM and 9 PM depending on the season.
eats.open_evidence: Own website says 'Celebrating 71 yrs in business! 1954 to 2025!' and lists current hours (viewed 2026-10-03).

eats.name: Red Iguana
eats.what_to_order: Any of its moles (the site lists Mole Negro, Amarillo, Poblano, Verde and more), plus the Killer Nachos.
eats.why: A Salt Lake City Mexican restaurant built around a long list of house moles, with two locations on the west side of downtown.
eats.hours_note: Sunday-Thursday 11 AM-9 PM; Friday and Saturday 11 AM-10 PM.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and the full mole menu, and cites a 2025 local-eats ranking (viewed 2026-10-03)

eats.name: Hires Big H
eats.what_to_order: A fresh-ground burger with fresh-cut fries, hand-dipped onion rings and the root beer the site calls 'Frosty'.
eats.why: A family-owned burger stand founded in 1959; the original location is at 425 S 700 E near downtown.
eats.hours_note: Closed Sundays; the site's pages give conflicting Friday and Saturday closing times, so confirm before going.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours and describes the founding commitment 'over 66 years ago' (1959), with the original location listed (viewed 2026-10-03); the pages carry no explicit 2026 date.

eats.name: The Eating Establishment
eats.what_to_order: Huevos rancheros or the shakshuka skillet, both named in the magazine's listing.
eats.why: A Main Street fixture since 1972 serving comfort food and breakfast, which is rare longevity on a street that turns over fast.
eats.open_evidence: Park City Magazine's restaurant guide, updated May 27, 2026, lists it at 317 Main St (viewed 2026-10-03); its own site could not be fetched.

eats.name: No Name Saloon & Grill
eats.what_to_order: The buffalo burger the site bills as 'World Famous'.
eats.why: A Main Street saloon in a building that dates to 1905, known for its buffalo burger.
eats.hours_note: Monday-Friday 11 AM-1 AM, Saturday-Sunday 10 AM-1 AM; no reservations; guests must be 21 or older (under-21s are directed to the Annex Burger next door).
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists current hours, menu and no-reservations policy (viewed 2026-10-03); the page carries no year.

eats.name: Bangkok Thai on Main
eats.what_to_order: Tom Kha Gai soup, Pad Thai, Kao Soi, Massaman Curry or Panang Curry, all named on the site.
eats.why: A Thai restaurant on Main Street open since 1994, which the site calls the only fine-dining Thai restaurant in Park City.
eats.hours_note: Own site lists 12-9 PM daily but a Park City restaurants listing shows different weekday hours, so confirm before going; reservations via Resy.
eats.open_evidence: Own website lists hours, a menu and a Resy reservation link, and mentions additions 'this summer' (viewed 2026-10-03); the page carries no explicit year.
